title: Open WebUI KatexRenderer -- T1059.007 stack-overflow fallback renders raw math source as HTML
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70492 (GHSA-pwxh-7358-jq2x,
CVSS 8.7 HIGH), affecting Open WebUI from 0.10.0 until 0.11.0.

`src/lib/components/chat/Messages/Markdown/KatexRenderer.svelte` could
store and render a chat message whose math block makes KaTeX fail with
a STACK OVERFLOW rather than an ordinary parse error. The component's
catch branch, written for the parse-error case, falls back to inserting
the original math source into the page via Svelte's `{@html}` directive
-- as raw HTML rather than as escaped text. A crafted math block that
deliberately triggers the stack-overflow path therefore executes
arbitrary script in the browser of ANYONE who views the message,
including shared chats and channels: the viewer's session token in
`localStorage` can be stolen, and if the viewer is an administrator,
their account can be taken over entirely.

Detection logic flags a stored chat message whose content contains both
a math-block delimiter (KaTeX/LaTeX's `$$` or `\(`/`\)`) and
script-injection markup within it -- the specific combination this
fallback path turns into executable HTML, distinct from an ordinary
malformed-but-inert math expression.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, which cites the exact component file and PR), fixed in
0.11.0.
